reviewed_record.name: Sites Optimizer setup
reviewed_record.src: Experience League: Sites Optimizer opportunity types
reviewed_record.basis: One site: Sites Optimizer connected, roles set, and the first SEO opportunities reviewed with the team.
reviewed_record.scope: Activate Sites Optimizer on the production site, connect Google Search Console, set who can deploy fixes and who can prepare code patches, and review the first SEO opportunities (broken backlinks, metadata, structured data, sitemap issues, Core Web Vitals) with the Client to agree what to fix first. Agree the route and owner for each kind of fix (authoring or source documents, code patches, or configuration such as redirects), deploy the first agreed content fixes (with Prime, apply them by hand) and prepare any code patches they need.
reviewed_record.deliverable: Configured Sites Optimizer, the roles and approvals model, the route and owner for each kind of fix, and a prioritized list of the first SEO fixes.
reviewed_record.acceptance: The Client can see and approve opportunities, each kind of fix has an agreed route and owner, the first agreed content fixes are in authoring (with Prime, applied by hand), and any code patches for them are with the named developer.
reviewed_record.assumptions:
The Client has licensed Sites Optimizer for AEM Sites (Edge Delivery, Cloud Service or Managed Services) and the site is a public production site. Hours scale with the number of sites.

How a fix is deployed depends on its opportunity. With the Ultimate package, approved content fixes go into authoring (on document-authored Edge Delivery sites, into the source documents) for people to review and publish, and Core Web Vitals fixes are prepared as code patches for a named developer who reviews, tests, merges and releases them. Deploying to authoring and preparing code patches each need the user's permission for that action and a fully configured site (Adobe's example is a connected code repository).

Code patches reach the developer as a pull request in the connected repository or as a downloaded patch; Adobe's October 2026 release notes list pull-request submission for Core Web Vitals as Early Access, so the route is confirmed here. On AEM as a Cloud Service sites, deploying broken-backlink redirects through Dispatcher is Early Access, used only where Adobe has enabled it.

With Prime, which identifies and suggests fixes, the first agreed content and configuration fixes are applied by hand and code fixes go to the named developer.

Core Web Vitals come from real-user data (Operational Telemetry, connected during setup if it isn't yet), and Adobe analyzes them only on pages with at least 1,000 page views.

Brand Visibility connects its own Search Console link; one access request to the Client covers both. Access for Adobe's scanner is confirmed here and its IP addresses are allowed in the CDN, firewall or Cloud Manager traffic filters.
reviewed_record.exclusions: The Sites Optimizer license, fixes outside the agreed opportunity types, and changes to systems outside AEM.

reviewed_record.name: Audiences that act on the data
reviewed_record.src: Experience League: Publish CJA audiences
reviewed_record.basis: One CJA data view: up to five audiences from AI-referred visitors, published to Real-Time Customer Profile, with an activation plan.
reviewed_record.scope: Define up to five audiences from AI-referred visits and their outcomes in the CJA data view, publish them to Real-Time Customer Profile, and agree with the Client how each audience is used in its existing channels.
reviewed_record.deliverable: Audience definitions, the published audiences, an activation plan with owners, and the measures to review in the monthly report.
reviewed_record.acceptance: The audiences populate in Real-Time Customer Profile with the agreed definitions, and the Client approves the activation plan.
reviewed_record.assumptions: The Client licenses Real-Time CDP or Journey Optimizer, because CJA audience publishing to Real-Time Customer Profile needs one of them; CJA alone does not license Profile Service. The Client has licensed CJA Select, Prime or Ultimate (derived fields are not included in CJA Foundation). A CJA administrator, who gets the Audience Publishing permission automatically, also has Experience Platform's Manage Profiles permission. The Person ID in the CJA connection is agreed: CJA sends it as each audience member's primary identity, one identity per person. Channel owners confirm identity, consent and the intended use, and take part. Any downstream destination is already configured and licensed in Experience Platform and is activated there after the audience is published. The source datasets don't need to be enabled for Profile. Audiences come from AI-referred visitors in the Client's existing web data, found with a derived field on AI referring domains; the Brand Visibility dataset holds only aggregate AI-agent activity by URL and host, with no personal identifiers, and is not needed for these audiences.
reviewed_record.exclusions: New destinations or channels, campaign production, personalization builds and audience work in other tools.

reviewed_record.name: CDN readiness and routing where required
reviewed_record.src: Experience League: Brand Visibility, Optimize at Edge
reviewed_record.basis: One Adobe Commerce store and its outer CDN: Optimize at Edge routing for AI agents, verified on one page.
reviewed_record.scope: Confirm how the store serves pages to AI agents and search engines and which CDN sits closest to visitors, since routing goes on that outer CDN. Prepare and test the Optimize at Edge routing rules for that CDN (Adobe's guides cover Fastly, Akamai, Cloudflare, CloudFront, Azure Front Door and Apache) and have the Client's CDN team, or the partner with delegated access, apply them in the agreed change window; allow Adobe's edge-optimization user agent through robots.txt and any firewall or bot-manager rules, keep the cache for AI agents separate, test failover to the origin and rollback, and verify one page before the first optimization goes live through the route.
reviewed_record.deliverable: The documented CDN topology and routing, the configured rules, the one-page verification, the rollback steps and the handoff of the verified route for the first edge deployment.
reviewed_record.acceptance: An approved optimization reaches AI agents through the Client's outer CDN on the verification page, people and search bots still get the origin page, rollback is tested, and the Client's hosting owner accepts the configuration.
reviewed_record.assumptions: The CDN topology, the routing owner and a change window are confirmed in week one: the partner prepares and tests the rules, the Client's CDN team (or the partner, with delegated access) applies them, and the hosting owner approves. Adobe documents self-serve routing only for AEM as a Cloud Service sites on Adobe's managed Fastly CDN and documents no edge route for Adobe Commerce on cloud infrastructure, so this plan puts the routing rules on the outer CDN (for a store served straight from Commerce's Fastly service, that service) and the partner confirms the route and effort with Adobe (abv-at-edge@adobe.com) before the change window. Where an existing setup is confirmed ready, this service confirms and verifies it.
reviewed_record.exclusions: CDN migration or new CDN contracts, replatforming, the optimizations deployed through the route (separate services) and store code changes.

reviewed_record.name: Implement Brand Concierge
reviewed_record.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge pre-go-live checklist and rollout plan
reviewed_record.basis: One Brand Concierge experience: approved content sources, conversation design for the agreed products, one handoff route, testing and launch on the agreed pages. Adobe's Brand Concierge FAQ puts a basic setup at about 3 to 5 days, an advanced implementation at about 2 to 4 weeks and go-live at about 6 to 9 weeks; these hours are a planning assumption for the work around that setup, not yet reconciled with Adobe's figures or an independent delivery estimate.
reviewed_record.scope: Set up the Brand Concierge experience for the agreed banking or insurance products: connect and curate the approved content sources, design the conversations and guardrails for the agreed questions, configure the brand voice and the required disclosures, set up the handoff (live chat, meeting booking or both) routed to one Client-designated team, build, with the Client's reviewers, the golden-answer test set (including the priority discovery questions from the Brand Visibility program) and the refusal and escalation scenarios, complete Adobe's pre-go-live checks, and launch on the agreed pages in stages.
reviewed_record.deliverable: A live Brand Concierge experience on the agreed pages; the source, guardrail and disclosure configuration; the golden-answer test set and results; the refusal and escalation scenarios; the completed pre-go-live checklist; and the launch and rollout record.
reviewed_record.acceptance: Client reviewers approve the sampled answers, disclosures and the handoff; the golden-answer set scores at or above the agreed level for correctness, helpfulness and brand fit, and the refusal and escalation scenarios pass; stakeholders sign off the pre-go-live checks; and the experience is live on the agreed pages, rolled out in the agreed stages.
reviewed_record.assumptions:
The Client has licensed Brand Concierge and supplies the approved content, current product facts, reviewers and the handoff destination; compliance decisions stay with the Client.

The documented handoff is live chat or meeting booking through Adobe Marketo Qualifier (formerly Sales Qualifier), which needs the representatives added as users in the Adobe Admin Console and at least one representative with a connected calendar (for meeting booking) or set live chat availability (for live chat); a handoff to another chat or contact-center platform is not a documented route and is confirmed with Adobe first.

Live chat and meeting booking don't need Marketo Engage: round robin and direct-agent routing work without it, and it is needed only for custom routing rules, which pick a team by Marketo attributes, and for writing concierge activities to the Marketo person record. Live chat conversations are kept for 30 days, so the Client confirms its own record-keeping needs.

The baseline is the anonymous, public-information experience; profile-based answers are not assumed. Hours scale with the number of products, sources, journeys and test conversations.

These hours cover the partner's work around Adobe's setup: approved sources and reviewers, conversation and disclosure design, the handoff, the golden-answer and refusal tests and the staged rollout.
reviewed_record.exclusions: New content, legal or compliance advice, a new chat or appointment platform, ongoing answer review (a separate service) and Coworker Skills.

reviewed_record.name: Automated optimization deployment pilot
reviewed_record.src: Experience League: Impact Measurement Engine
reviewed_record.basis: One deployment of 20 to 50 eligible URLs on an agreed Optimize at Edge route.
reviewed_record.scope: Using the agreed Optimize at Edge route, check that each selected page sends a Last-Modified header where the opportunity needs one, then deploy approved changes for one supported opportunity type (such as Recover Content Visibility, Add Table of Contents or Add LLM-friendly Summaries) to 20 to 50 URLs chosen with the High Potential URLs filter, in one deployment; verify rollback; keep those pages unchanged during the measurement period; and run two operator sessions. Review the Impact Measurement Engine's analysis with the Client if Adobe generates one.
reviewed_record.deliverable: Validated deployment pilot, release and rollback checklist, operator handover, and the Impact Measurement Engine's impact analysis when Adobe generates one for the deployment.
reviewed_record.acceptance: Approved pilot changes deploy successfully, rollback is verified and the Client accepts release ownership. The impact analysis is reviewed when available; it is not an acceptance condition, because Adobe generates it only for eligible deployments and measures only pages with enough data, using a representative subset of the URLs.
reviewed_record.assumptions: The Client has an eligible deployment route (Optimize at Edge routing on the outer CDN: already in place; set up self-serve in Brand Visibility, as part of this pilot, for AEM as a Cloud Service sites on Adobe's managed Fastly CDN (where Implement AEM Sites on Edge Delivery is part of this engagement, it turns the route on); applied by the Client's CDN team; or set up by CDN readiness and routing), access, capacity and approved changes. Where routing covers only some paths, the selected URLs are inside them. Trial workspaces have tighter deployment limits (Adobe's pages give 10 pages, or 50 URLs for trials from April 1, 2026), so the paid offer is assumed. Adobe lists edge auto-optimization as Early Access for select opportunities, so the opportunity type is confirmed for the Client. Adobe generates an impact analysis only for eligible deployments: a supported opportunity type and at least 20 URLs from the High Potential URLs filter in a single deployment. Recover Content Visibility results typically take about two weeks. For content opportunities such as Add LLM-friendly Summaries, Brand Visibility watches the source page's Last-Modified response header: it pauses the optimization for review when the page changes and skips it when the header is missing. A selected page without the header is replaced, or the Client's team adds the header before deployment.
reviewed_record.exclusions: Custom connectors, CDN migration, ongoing optimization and pilot work already included in another selected service.

definitions.Direct support: The current source set supports the material product capability and service fit. Partner quantities, hours and delivery methods still require engagement-specific scoping.
definitions.Partial support: The current source set supports a meaningful portion, but another material part, limitation or prerequisite needs a better citation or clearer wording.
definitions.Background only: The linked material concerns the product or adjacent capability but does not substantiate the core work as described.
definitions.No supporting source found: No adequate attached or researched support was recorded. Generic partner advisory work can still be valid without an Adobe capability claim.
definitions.Unable to verify: The evidence could not be adequately retrieved or resolved; no positive or negative capability conclusion is certified.

verification.independent_content_review: High-priority findings and selected citation-gap judgments received a second review against original scope and existing qualifications. Corrections were reconciled before publication.
